brief.headline: The exchange stayed shut for a third day, so the price did not move - but the two things this desk flagged as unresolved on Sunday both resolved, and they resolved in opposite directions: oil finally priced the Hormuz escalation and is up for a third straight session above $84, while Tehran itself said in public that the Oman route deal will NOT reopen the strait and rejected direct talks with Washington for now.
bullets: WHAT MOVED ON THE EXCHANGE: NOTHING, AND THAT IS STILL THE HONEST STARTING POINT. THE LME BOARD ON THIS PAGE IS THE 07-AUGUST OFFICIAL CARRIED FORWARD FOR A THIRD CALENDAR DAY. These are carried figures, not new ones. The first genuinely new aluminium price information of the week arrives at 13:20 London today.

WHAT DID MOVE IS THE COST FLOOR, AND IT MOVED THE WAY SUNDAY'S REPORT SAID IT WOULD. Sunday's note flagged an explicit asymmetry - that the oil market had closed the week LOWER on de-escalation optimism and had not yet priced the weekend escalation. It has now. Brent traded above $84 on Monday, a THIRD consecutive session of gains, last around $84.50 (+1.13%), with the settled 10-August mark at $84.27 (+0.86%); WTI is near $78.89 (+0.91%) and European TTF gas near EUR 56.46 (+1.65%). Trading Economics attributes the move directly to Hormuz uncertainty. Energy is 30-40% of smelter cash cost - more than every other input on this board combined - so a three-session energy advance raises the industry cost floor, feeds calcined petroleum coke and coal tar pitch with a lag, and feeds bauxite freight immediately. This is the clearest bullish-cost datapoint of the last 72 hours and it required no LME session to happen.

THE GEOPOLITICAL TAPE GOT WORSE ON BOTH LEGS OVER SUNDAY, AND THE SECOND LEG IS THE ONE THE MARKET KEEPS UNDER-PRICING. On Hormuz, Iran said talks with Oman on a shipping route were nearing agreement but warned that any arrangement would NOT produce an immediate reopening, rejected direct negotiations with the United States for now citing breaches of the June interim deal, and held to its demands - an end to the US naval blockade, sanctions relief and compensation for war damage. That is Tehran itself confirming the decoupling the IRGC stated on Saturday. On the Red Sea, which is a SEPARATE corridor the Oman arrangement does not touch at all, Houthi forces struck Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery with a drone early on Sunday 09-August; the Saudi energy ministry said the fire was extinguished with no injuries. The attack came two days after Saudi Arabia signed a defence pact with Turkey and Pakistan, and the group also claimed an attack on a Yemeni port. Bab al-Mandeb is the leg that carries Gulf and Asian metal into Rotterdam via Suez.

WHAT TO WATCH TODAY, IN ORDER OF INFORMATION VALUE. (1) The 13:20 London official and specifically the CASH-3M SPREAD: four sessions have now passed without a prompt premium, two of them outright contangos, on a warehouse at a century low. If the spread still refuses to bid with a missile strike inside the strait, a refinery hit in Jazan and oil up three sessions on the tape, the conclusion stops being ambiguous - the front-month scarcity in this rally was a corridor artefact and the flat price is borrowing entirely against a forward deficit that is already well priced. (2) Whether exchange stock posts its FIRST BUILD in 29 sessions, which would matter more than another draw. (3) The single most bearish item on the tape is unconfirmed and worth respecting: reports after Friday's settlement that the US could lift its naval blockade once commercial shipping through the strait resumes without restrictions. Treat that as reported information, not fact - but the 17-June precedent, official cash falling 20.6% from $3,855.00 to $3,061.50 on a ceasefire, is on the record.

lme.commentary: NO NEW LME PRICE INFORMATION EXISTS AT THIS COMPILE AND THE BOARD IS LABELLED ACCORDINGLY. There was no session on Saturday 08-August or Sunday 09-August, and this report is produced at roughly 03:35 London on Monday 10-August, ahead of the 13:20 ring. Everything on this page is the 07-August official carried into a third calendar day: cash $3,279.50 (+$18.50, +0.57%), 3-month $3,280.00 (+$20.00, +0.61%), stock 256,400 t (-1,500 t). Both price legs are the highest since 22-June-2026 and stock is the lowest this century after a 28th consecutive draw. THE STRUCTURE IS STILL THE STORY AND IT STILL POINTS THE OTHER WAY. Cash settled BELOW the 3-month, a $0.50 CONTANGO - the second in three sessions - because the forward leg rose more than the prompt. The August sequence reads +$48.00, +$34.50, a $0.50 CONTANGO, +$1.00 and a $0.50 CONTANGO. Roughly $35/t of front-month structure was written off on the 05-August routing announcement and none of it has come back across four sessions. A seven-week high in flat price alongside a contango, on a warehouse at its lowest level this century, is an explicit statement that nobody is paying up for metal today. WHAT HAS CHANGED SINCE THAT PRINT, AND IT IS NOT NOTHING. Two pieces of information have landed that the front of this curve has not had the chance to price. First, the cost floor rose: Brent is up for a THIRD consecutive session above $84 - $84.27 (+0.86%) with intraday trade near $84.50 - explicitly on Hormuz uncertainty, WTI near $78.89 and European TTF gas near EUR 56.46 (+1.65%). The prior run flagged that oil had not yet priced the weekend escalation; it now has. Second, the diplomatic assumption behind the 05-August contango was contradicted at two levels of the Iranian state inside 24 hours - the IRGC on Saturday and the government on Sunday, both saying the Oman route arrangement does not reopen the strait. Against that sits one genuinely bearish and UNCONFIRMED report from Friday's post-settlement trade, that the US could lift its naval blockade once commercial shipping resumes without restrictions. THE TEST IS TODAY AT 13:20. If the cash-3M spread still refuses to bid past $20-30 with a missile strike inside the strait, a refinery hit at Jazan and oil up three sessions on the tape, the front-month scarcity in this rally can fairly be called a corridor artefact that has been written to zero - and the flat price would be borrowing entirely against a forward deficit that is already well priced. Watch the stock line too: a first BUILD in 29 sessions would carry more information than another draw.

Since Friday's close the tape has produced a missile strike on a commercial vessel inside the strait, an explicit Iranian statement that the route deal is not a reopening, a Houthi drone strike on Aramco's Jazan refinery and three consecutive sessions of oil gains. If the spread still declines to bid at 13:20 today, that is a strong buyers' argument for the Q4 MJP negotiation and a weak signal for prompt physical tightness generally.

drivers.text: THE US PREMIUM IS MOSTLY TARIFF, AND THE DECOMPOSITION IS ARITHMETIC ON PUBLIC INPUTS RATHER THAN AN ASSESSMENT — Section 232 stands at 50% ad valorem on aluminium articles and 25% on listed derivatives, applied since 06-April-2026 to the FULL customs value of covered articles regardless of metal content, with Annex I-C carve-outs at 15% for Japan, Korea, the UK, Switzerland, Taiwan and the EU. On the carried 07-August official cash of $3,279.50 the mechanical tariff leg is $1,639.75/t against a US Midwest duty-paid quotation of $2,380/t - so the tariff accounts for roughly 69% of the delivered US premium and the residual market premium is about $740/t. No split of that residual into freight, financing and tightness is published here, because no public assessment supports one and fabricating one would be worse than leaving the gap.

drivers.text: THE EUROPEAN DELIVERED CHAIN IS CONSTRAINED BY A CORRIDOR THE HORMUZ ARRANGEMENT DOES NOT TOUCH — The Bab al-Mandeb and Red Sea leg carries Gulf and Asian metal into Rotterdam via Suez and is impaired independently of the Strait of Hormuz. It deteriorated again on 09-August when Houthi forces struck Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery with a drone - fire extinguished, no injuries per the Saudi energy ministry - two days after Saudi Arabia signed a defence pact with Turkey and Pakistan, and the group also claimed an attack on a Yemeni port. Simultaneous disruption at both chokepoints forces routing via the Cape of Good Hope, lengthening transit and raising freight and insurance. Even a full Hormuz reopening would not restore this leg, which is a structural support for European duty-paid quotations that the flat-price narrative tends to ignore.
drivers.source: Al Jazeera - Saudi Arabia says fire extinguished at Aramco facility in Jizan (09-Aug-2026)

drivers.text: FREIGHT IS RISING INDEPENDENTLY OF GEOPOLITICS AND A REOPENING WOULD NOT REVERSE IT — The Baltic Dry Index reached 3,089 on 07-August, up 32 points and a SIXTH consecutive gain, extending a run from 2,732 on 01-August through 2,843, 2,936 and 3,063. Guinea-to-China bauxite freight is separately running up to about $35/mt on higher bunker costs, and Brent has now risen for three consecutive sessions above $84, which feeds bunkers directly. Dry-bulk freight strength is a delivered-cost increment on bauxite and alumina into China and on ingot into Europe, it is not a function of the Hormuz corridor, and it puts a floor under delivered premiums that a diplomatic outcome would not remove.

logistics.label: Strait of Hormuz transit
logistics.note: Iran and Oman agreed the coordinates of a proposed routing on 05-August - a northern inbound lane in Iranian territorial waters and a southern outbound lane in Omani waters, initially 60 days and extendable - but the joint statement remains unsigned with no start date. Over the weekend the framing hardened at two levels of the Iranian state: an IRGC spokesman said on 08-August that reopening 'has its own specific mechanism and has nothing to do with the negotiations between Iran and Oman', and on 09-August Tehran said the talks were nearing agreement but warned any arrangement would NOT produce an immediate reopening, rejected direct US negotiations for now citing breaches of the June interim deal, and held to demands for an end to the US naval blockade, sanctions relief and compensation. A missile struck an ADNOC vessel inside the strait on 08-August; ADNOC says 15 of its vessels have been attacked since the conflict began, three of them that week. Kpler reports only a handful of transits daily, usually fewer than ten, against roughly 130 a day pre-war.

logistics.label: Red Sea / Bab al Mandeb corridor
logistics.note: The Bab al-Mandeb leg that carries Gulf and Asian metal into Rotterdam via Suez remains impaired INDEPENDENTLY of the Strait of Hormuz and is not addressed by the Iran-Oman arrangement at all. It deteriorated again over the weekend: Houthi forces struck Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery with a drone early on Sunday 09-August - fire extinguished, no injuries per the Saudi energy ministry - framed as retaliation for alleged Saudi drone incursions over Saada and Hajjah and coming two days after Saudi Arabia signed a defence pact with Turkey and Pakistan. The group also claimed an attack on a Yemeni port, and had struck Marib and Najran in the preceding days. Simultaneous disruption at both chokepoints forces routing via the Cape of Good Hope, lengthening transit and raising freight and insurance. Even a full Hormuz reopening would not restore this leg.

logistics.label: Gulf war-risk insurance
logistics.note: WAR-RISK COVER FOR GULF TRANSITS REMAINS QUOTED AT 3-10% OF HULL VALUE, with recent quotes clustering at the 7.5-10% end, against roughly 0.25% before hostilities - a 12-to-40-fold increase that is a direct, publicly observable addition to the delivered cost of every tonne moving out of the Gulf. NOTHING THIS WEEKEND ARGUES FOR A RE-RATING DOWN, AND SATURDAY'S MISSILE STRIKE ON AN ADNOC VESSEL INSIDE THE STRAIT ARGUES THE OTHER WAY. Underwriters price observed attack frequency, not diplomatic communiques; three vessels of a single operator attacked inside one week is the kind of loss experience that sustains or widens quoted rates regardless of whether a route agreement is signed. This premium is one of the clearest reasons why regional physical premiums have not retraced with the LME prompt spread.

logistics.label: Container freight (Drewry WCI)

Direction is easing, but several carriers filed Emergency Fuel Surcharges effective August 2026 on continued Hormuz disruption, so realised container cost falls more slowly than the index and August invoices now carry those surcharges. With Brent back up 2.85% on 04-Aug, the bunker input under those surcharges is rising again.

logistics.label: Incoterms / demurrage
logistics.note: EGA's force majeure on European billet contracts, declared 12-Apr-2026, was still in force at the last public check on 20-Jul. War-risk and cancellation clauses across roughly 90% of International Group P&I tonnage remain repriceable on short notice. THE PRACTICAL POINT FOR CONTRACTING: the 48-hour swing from claimed deal perimeters to a public accusation of duplicity and a fresh vessel strike is exactly the volatility that keeps force-majeure and war-risk language live in Gulf-origin contracts, regardless of which way the next headline points.

row.note: BRENT CLIMBED ABOVE $84/bbl ON MONDAY FOR A THIRD CONSECUTIVE SESSION OF GAINS, marking the 10-August level at $84.27 (+0.86% on the prior settle) and trading around $84.50 (+1.13%) intraday; WTI is near $78.89 (+0.91%). THIS IS THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT RESOLVED QUESTION ON THE BOARD. The prior run flagged an explicit asymmetry - that Brent had closed the WEEK LOWER on Hormuz de-escalation optimism and had not yet priced the weekend escalation. It has now priced it, and Trading Economics attributes the third straight advance directly to Hormuz uncertainty: Iran warning that the Oman route arrangement will not produce an immediate reopening, Tehran rejecting direct US negotiations for now, a Houthi drone strike on Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery on Sunday, and the ADNOC vessel attacked inside the strait on Saturday. WHY IT MATTERS FOR ALUMINIUM: energy is 30-40% of smelter cash cost, more than every other input on this board combined, so a three-session advance lifts the industry cost floor and preserves supply discipline. It also feeds the calcined-petroleum-coke and coal-tar-pitch legs of the carbon block with a lag, and it feeds freight directly - Guinea-to-China bauxite freight is already running up to about $35/mt on higher bunker costs.

row.label: European gas TTF

At EUR 56/MWh the level remains far below the 2022 crisis and does not on its own threaten the announced restarts, all of which are underpinned by long-term contracts, state-utility arrangements and EU ETS indirect-cost compensation rather than spot gas. The direction has now turned back UP after the early-August fall, which marginally raises the cost of the restart pipeline without changing its feasibility.

ADNOC states that 15 of its vessels have been attacked by missiles and drones while transiting the strait since the start of the conflict, INCLUDING THREE IN THAT WEEK, killing one crew member and injuring 20. The UAE foreign ministry said targeting commercial shipping and using the strait as a tool of economic coercion constitutes acts of piracy by the IRGC and a direct threat to regional stability and global energy security.

events.note: TRANSIT COUNTS REMAIN FAR BELOW PRE-WAR LEVELS. Shipping analysts Kpler report only a handful of vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz daily, usually fewer than ten, against roughly 130 a day in peacetime; some ships have switched off transponders to avoid detection. The reported route structure is unchanged - a northern inbound lane in Iranian territorial waters and a southern outbound lane in Omani waters, envisaged initially for 60 days and extendable, with mine clearance of a central corridor, military passage and a possible coordinated transit fee still under discussion. No measurable change in any physical observable has followed the 05-August announcement.

headlines.title: THE COST FLOOR HAS NOW PRICED THE ESCALATION - BRENT UP A THIRD CONSECUTIVE SESSION ABOVE $84. Brent marked $84.27 on 10-August (+0.86%) and traded near $84.50 (+1.13%), WTI near $78.89 (+0.91%) and European TTF gas near EUR 56.46 (+1.65%), with Trading Economics attributing the run directly to Hormuz uncertainty. This is the resolution of an asymmetry the prior run flagged explicitly: the oil market had closed the week LOWER on de-escalation optimism and had not yet priced Saturday's missile strike. Energy is 30-40% of smelter cash cost - more than every other input on this board combined - so three sessions of gains lift the industry cost floor, feed calcined petroleum coke and coal tar pitch with a lag, and feed bauxite freight immediately.

THE RED SEA LEG DETERIORATED AGAIN AND IS NOT ADDRESSED BY THE OMAN ARRANGEMENT. Houthi forces struck Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery with a drone early on Sunday 09-August; the Saudi energy ministry said the fire was extinguished with no injuries. The group framed it as retaliation for alleged Saudi drone incursions over Saada and Hajjah, and it came two days after Saudi Arabia signed a defence pact with Turkey and Pakistan. The Houthis also claimed an attack on a Yemeni port. Bab al-Mandeb is the corridor that carries Gulf and Asian metal into Rotterdam via Suez, and it is a SEPARATE problem from the Strait of Hormuz: even a full Hormuz reopening would not restore the European delivered chain. The Baltic Dry Index reinforces the point at 3,089 on 07-August, a sixth consecutive gain.

TEHRAN CONFIRMED IN PUBLIC THAT THE ROUTE DEAL IS NOT A REOPENING. Iran said over the weekend that talks with Oman were nearing agreement but warned that any arrangement would NOT lead to an immediate reopening of the strait, rejected direct negotiations with the United States for now citing breaches of the June interim deal, and held to its demands - an end to the US naval blockade, sanctions relief and compensation for war damages. Read with Saturday's IRGC statement that reopening 'has its own specific mechanism and has nothing to do with the negotiations between Iran and Oman', this is a consistent position stated at two levels of the Iranian state inside 24 hours. The LME curve wrote off roughly $35/t of prompt structure on 05-August on the opposite assumption.

THE COUNTERWEIGHT, LABELLED HONESTLY AS UNCONFIRMED: oil reversed some of Friday's gains in post-settlement trading after reports that the US COULD LIFT ITS NAVAL BLOCKADE once commercial shipping through the strait resumes without restrictions. This is reported information rather than announced policy, and Tehran's weekend statements point the other way, but it deserves weight because removal of the blockade is on Iran's own account the actual reopening trigger and sits on a separate track from the Oman route negotiation. The precedent is on the official record: on the 17-June ceasefire, LME official cash fell from $3,855.00 to $3,061.50, -20.6%.

A SEVEN-WEEK HIGH THE CURVE DECLINED TO CONFIRM, NOW CARRIED THROUGH A CLOSED WEEKEND AND INTO A THIRD CALENDAR DAY. The 07-August official settled cash $3,279.50 (+$18.50) and 3M $3,280.00 (+$20.00), the highest since 22-June-2026 - but the forward leg rose more than cash, so the curve slipped into a $0.50 CONTANGO, the second in three sessions. Stock fell 1,500 t to 256,400 t, a 28th consecutive draw and the lowest this century. Four sessions have now passed without a prompt premium. The next officials print at 13:20 London today and the spread is the single highest-information number on that board.

THE DATED AND FUNDED RESTART PIPELINE IS UNCHANGED AND REMAINS THE STRONGEST BEARISH ARGUMENT THAT DOES NOT DEPEND ON GEOPOLITICS. Slovalco is restarting 75,000 t targeted for Q4-2026 with roughly EUR 100m of investment, a long-term state-utility power contract and EU ETS indirect-cost compensation. Magnitude 7 Metals confirmed in early-August reporting that it expects to restart its Marston, Missouri smelter before year-end - about 75,000 t on the first potline - though it has not disclosed how it will power the site or given a specific timeline, and local environmental groups have raised sulphur-dioxide objections. Century's Mt. Holly is at full capacity for the first time since 2015 and Grundartangi Line 2 is near full; EGA continues restoring Al Taweelah cell by cell.

PEER SEASON MESSAGE IS ABOUT INTEGRATION, NOT PRICE, AND THE GULF DIVERSIFIED PRINT FITS THE PATTERN. Maaden (1211) reported Q2-2026 net profit of SAR 2.18bn, up 13% year-on-year and 33% quarter-on-quarter, on revenue of SAR 10.9bn (+16% y/y, +24% q/q), with the company citing higher commodity prices across all business units and higher aluminium and gold sales volumes - but gross profit FELL 4% to SAR 3.39bn and operating profit fell 8% to SAR 2.36bn on higher phosphate logistics and raw-material costs including sulphur. That is the same split visible at Hindalco (record integrated upstream EBITDA) and Century (raw-material realisation as the principal headwind): a rising metal price is not converting one-for-one into margin where the input leg is bought rather than owned.

THE RAW-MATERIAL LEG HAS NOT STOPPED RISING AND THE ENERGY LEG HAS NOW REJOINED IT. SMM's imported bauxite index reached $71.57/mt on 06-August, up $0.70 week-on-week, with Guinea sellers at $72-73 against Chinese refinery bids of $70-71 and August long-term contracts unsettled and rumoured higher; freight to China is running up to about $35/mt; 30,000 mt of alumina transacted at $356/mt FOB East Australia on 05-August. With Brent up three sessions and TTF up 1.65%, both legs of the cost stack are now moving the same way for the first time in a week. The Baltic Dry Index at 3,089 on 07-August adds a freight increment that a Hormuz reopening would not reverse.

THE POLICY CEILING IS STILL DOING MORE WORK THAN DEMAND. China's primary output reached 45.02 Mt in 2025 against the self-imposed 45 Mt cap, with H1-2026 at 22.34 Mt, and industry commentary describes room for further expansion as effectively exhausted. On the demand side the official NBS manufacturing PMI is in contraction at 49.2 against the private RatingDog gauge at 50.9, and the high-temperature off-season is cutting cast-alloy operating rates. Net exports are down roughly 700,000 t year-to-date, which is why weak Chinese demand now depresses Chinese premiums more than it depresses the LME - the metal is not leaving in the volumes it used to. Shanghai equities gained 1.02% on Monday, a risk-tone positive rather than a demand datapoint.

SECTION 232 VERIFIED UNCHANGED THIS RUN AT 50% ON ALUMINIUM ARTICLES AND 25% ON LISTED DERIVATIVES, applied since 06-April-2026 to the full customs value of covered articles regardless of metal content, with Annex I-C carve-outs at 15% for Japan, Korea, the UK, Switzerland, Taiwan and the EU. On the carried 07-August cash of $3,279.50 the mechanical tariff leg is therefore $1,639.75/t against a US Midwest duty-paid quotation of $2,380/t - meaning the tariff accounts for roughly 69% of the delivered US premium and the residual market premium is about $740/t. That decomposition is arithmetic on public inputs, not an assessment of freight, financing or tightness.

earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

Management explicitly framed the curtailments as preserving flexibility for a swift recovery when conditions improve, which is the restart option the bearish case depends on. Separately Alba is progressing its US$2.2bn acquisition of Aluminium Dunkerque, about 300,000 t/y and the largest EU smelter.

China's net aluminium exports are down roughly 700,000 t year-to-date. An open policy question is whether renewable-powered smelters should be exempt from the cap. trade.note: REVIEWED 09-August-2026. THE CORRIDOR REGIME IS UNCHANGED AND THE WEEKEND MOVED IT AWAY FROM NORMALISATION RATHER THAN TOWARD IT, so no flow row is re-rated: the Iran-Oman routing coordinates agreed 05-August remain unsigned with no start date, an IRGC spokesman stated on 08-August that reopening is mechanically separate from the Oman talks, and an ADNOC vessel was struck by a missile inside the strait in the early hours of 08-August. Bab al-Mandeb deteriorated independently on renewed Houthi activity. These flows are reviewed monthly or on material change and are not churned daily; the next scheduled re-rating trigger is a signed joint statement with a start date, a change in the US naval blockade, or a tariff change. UPDATED 10-AUG-2026 ON A MATERIAL CHANGE TO THE RED SEA LEG RATHER THAN A ROUTINE DAILY CHURN: Houthi forces struck Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery with a drone in the early hours of 09-August - fire extinguished with no injuries per the Saudi energy ministry - two days after Saudi Arabia signed a defence pact with Turkey and Pakistan, and the group separately claimed an attack on a Yemeni port. Separately, on 09-August Tehran said the Oman route talks were nearing agreement but warned any arrangement would NOT produce an immediate reopening of Hormuz and rejected direct US negotiations for now. Neither corridor's regime has actually changed; both have hardened.

flows.note: About 9% of global primary supply exits via the Strait of Hormuz and more than 80% of Gulf metal is exported; Gulf output was -34.5% y/y in June, and on the published aggregate the IAI's June-2026 release (20-July-2026) showed global primary output down 1.5% y/y; a widely repeated 'outside-China -6.7% y/y in July' figure could not be traced to a dated IAI release at this refresh and is not carried here. Transit has been the binding constraint rather than production - but production is also impaired in its own right: EGA at 89 of 1,262 pots on 02-Jul and Alba's Lines 1-3 (19% of 1,623,000 t/y) shut since 15-Mar and confirmed still shut in its 04-Aug Q2 disclosure. THE 05-AUG IRAN-OMAN AGREEMENT ON ROUTE COORDINATES IS THE FIRST CONCRETE STEP TOWARD A REOPENING, and it is deliberately NOT treated as one here: the route is temporary (two to four months by Iran's own account), both existing lanes would close in its favour, Tehran says safe navigation is not restored, and the published count on the day was eight vessels against roughly 130-140 pre-war. Kept at 'tightening' pending observable transit recovery. Even a full transit reopening leaves the production impairment in place for quarters.

flows.note: THE RED SEA IS DIVERGING FROM HORMUZ. Bab al Mandeb traffic fell to a weekly low of 16 commodity vessels on 26-Jul after the Houthi 'embargo' on Saudi shipping declared 20-Jul and claimed attacks on Aramco sites at Jizan and Yanbu, recovering only to 31 by 31-Jul. On 05-Aug Houthi forces claimed they had targeted a Saudi oil tanker in the Gulf of Aden and threatened further vessels in the Red Sea, with a ship reported hit the same day. A Hormuz routing agreement does not address this constraint. Saudi Arabia has been diverting crude to the Suez routing; the Suez leg for Gulf and Red Sea origin cargoes is therefore still not a clean alternative to Hormuz.

catalysts.text: THE 10-AUGUST LME OFFICIAL - THE FIRST GENUINELY NEW ALUMINIUM PRICE INFORMATION SINCE FRIDAY AND A HIGHER-INFORMATION EVENT THAN A NORMAL RING, because it prices three calendar days of accumulated news at once. Three reads in order of value: (1) does the cash-3M spread rebuild into a backwardation past $20-30 given the 08-August missile strike, Tehran's own 09-August statement that the Oman arrangement does not reopen the strait, the Jazan refinery attack and three consecutive sessions of oil gains - or does contango hold as the default state of a market on century-low inventory? The latter, with that tape, would confirm the front-month scarcity of this rally was a corridor artefact. (2) Does exchange stock post its FIRST BUILD in 29 sessions, which would be far more significant than another draw? (3) Does the 3M hold above the $3,229.50 short-term Elliott-wave invalidation, $50.50 below the carried 07-Aug close?

CONFIRMED MOVEMENT ON THE US NAVAL BLOCKADE, WHICH ON TEHRAN'S OWN ACCOUNT IS THE ACTUAL REOPENING TRIGGER AND IS NOW THE SINGLE MOST BEARISH ITEM ON THE TAPE. Reports after Friday's settlement suggested the US could lift the blockade once commercial shipping through the strait resumes without restrictions; that is REPORTED INFORMATION, not announced policy, and Tehran's weekend statements point the other way. Iran's stated preconditions for reopening run to lifting the blockade, a drawback of US military assets, a permanent end to the war, compensation for war damage and release of frozen assets - a separate track from the Oman route negotiation, explicitly identified as such by both the foreign ministry and the IRGC. Any confirmed concession on the blockade or force posture is the headline most likely to reprice the physical market, and it is not on any scheduled calendar.

SIGNATURE OF THE IRAN-OMAN JOINT STATEMENT WITH A START DATE - BUT THE WEEKEND MATERIALLY WEAKENED THIS AS A TRIGGER. The coordinates were agreed 05-August and the statement covering technical, legal, security and environmental points remains in final drafting, with the Iranian parliament's national security commission saying the framework awaits a green light from 'higher levels'. On 08-August the IRGC said reopening 'has its own specific mechanism and has nothing to do with the negotiations between Iran and Oman', and on 09-August the government itself said any arrangement would not produce an immediate reopening. A signature may therefore now be a weaker trigger than the market assumed on 05-August, when the announcement alone removed $42.00 from cash and roughly $35/t of prompt structure. Watch the observables rather than the headline: transit counts, war-risk quotes, and any announced Gulf smelter restart.

SMM BAUXITE WEEKLY REVIEW. The imported bauxite index reached $71.57/mt on 06-August, up $0.70 week-on-week, with Guinea sellers at $72-73 against Chinese refinery bids of $70-71. This is the most current hard input mark on the board and it has risen every week for several weeks. With Brent up three sessions, freight and feedstock pressures now point the same way.

SMM FLUORIDE-SALT, SILICON AND MAGNESIUM WEEKLY REVIEWS. Silicon and magnesium last printed 06-August (#553 at RMB 9,000-9,100/t flat week-on-week; magnesium RMB 15,800-15,900/t at Fugu and Shenmu, Tianjin FOB $2,240-2,340). AlF3 and cryolite have not carried a public weekly since 25-June and those rows remain carried at that date rather than rolled. No new marks published over the weekend, so no sparkline points were appended this run.

AUGUST GUINEA LONG-TERM BAUXITE CONTRACT SETTLEMENT. July settled at $70-71.5/mt; August contracts remain under negotiation and are rumoured higher. This is the next scheduled hard datapoint for the raw-material leg of the cost stack and it feeds directly into the alumina cost curve.

AUGUST-2026 PREBAKED ANODE AND COAL TAR PITCH SETTLEMENT CYCLE. Both price on monthly cycles that publish around the 17th-18th. The last valid marks are the July-2026 Shandong benchmark at RMB 5,683/t and the June-2026 modified coal tar pitch cycle at RMB 4,940/t in Shanxi. Green petcoke 3B settles on the same rhythm and drives the CPC row's feedstock sparkline. Three consecutive sessions of crude gains are a forward pressure on this cycle rather than a present one.

CHINA JULY TRADE AND INDUSTRIAL OUTPUT DATA, plus the monthly primary aluminium production print, and separately the International Aluminium Institute's July release due around the 20th. The June IAI release published on 20-July showed global primary output down 1.5% year-on-year. The key questions are whether Chinese output is genuinely pinned at the 45 Mt annualised ceiling (2025 actual 45.02 Mt, H1-2026 22.34 Mt) and whether net exports extend the roughly 700,000 t year-to-date decline.

OPENING OF THE Q4-2026 MJP PREMIUM NEGOTIATION. Talks normally open around late August and conclude late September, off an 11-year-high Q3 settlement of $395/t CIF Japan. The buyers' case rests on four sessions without a prompt premium and a yen near 158; the sellers' case rests on century-low exchange stock, curtailed Gulf capacity and a weekend that produced a missile strike inside the strait, a refinery attack at Jazan and an explicit Iranian statement that the route deal is not a reopening. The scenario range carried on this board is $315-415 and is a construct, not an assessment.

CHALCO H1-2026 INTERIM RESULTS, expected late August, which is the next scheduled addition to the per-company earnings-history strips. Chalco publishes cumulative net profit attributable rather than quarterly figures and no EBITDA line in any period, so Q2-2026 will be derived arithmetically from published totals and labelled as such. The strip currently runs Q3-25, Q4-25 and Q1-26 with Q2-26 left as an honest gap.

REMAINING PEER DISCLOSURES AND OPERATIONAL UPDATES - in particular any further detail on EGA's Al Taweelah cell restart count, Alba's guidance on when Lines 1-3 return, and confirmation of the Slovalco Q4-2026 restart date and the Magnitude 7 New Madrid timeline and power arrangement. Roughly 150,000 t of announced Western restarts is scheduled to land in or shortly after Q4.

FOMC WITH UPDATED DOTS. The Fed held 9-3 on 29-July with three dissents FOR a hike. June core PCE at +0.1% month-on-month and 3.3% year-on-year leans dovish, and a soft US jobs print has since kept the dollar on the back foot at about 99.67 with gold and silver holding gains. A hawkish surprise would lift the dollar and weigh on dollar-denominated metal; the three-session energy rally is the main argument on the other side of the inflation arithmetic.

risks.text: THE PROMPT PREMIUM HAS NOW FAILED TO REBUILD FOR FOUR CONSECUTIVE SESSIONS AND TODAY IS THE CLEAN TEST. The cash-3M sequence for August reads +$48.00, +$34.50, a $0.50 CONTANGO, +$1.00 and a $0.50 CONTANGO again. The 07-August official put flat price at a seven-week high WHILE the structure moved the other way, and 28 consecutive warehouse draws to the lowest exchange inventory this century have produced no prompt premium whatsoever. Roughly $35/t of front-month structure was written off on the 05-August routing announcement - that is, on an assumption that the corridor was normalising. THE WEEKEND SUPPLIED THREE PIECES OF EVIDENCE AGAINST THAT ASSUMPTION: a missile strike on a commercial vessel inside the strait on 08-August, an IRGC statement decoupling reopening from the Oman talks, and on 09-August the Iranian government itself warning that any route arrangement would not produce an immediate reopening while rejecting direct US negotiations. Oil has priced all of it - three consecutive sessions higher. If the prompt spread still refuses to bid at 13:20 today with that on the tape, the conclusion is no longer ambiguous: the front-month scarcity of this rally was a corridor artefact, it has been written to zero, and the flat-price advance is borrowing entirely against a forward deficit that is already well priced. WHAT WOULD FALSIFY IT: a backwardation rebuilding past $20-30 on the 10-August official while stock continues to draw.

SUPPLY IS RETURNING ON A DATED AND FUNDED SCHEDULE AND THIS REMAINS THE STRONGEST BEARISH ARGUMENT THAT DOES NOT DEPEND ON GEOPOLITICS AT ALL. Slovalco will restart 75,000 t with production targeted in Q4-2026, backed by roughly EUR 100m of investment, a long-term state-utility power contract and EU ETS indirect-cost compensation. Magnitude 7 Metals confirmed in early-August reporting that it expects to restart its Marston, Missouri smelter before year-end - about 75,000 t on the first potline - explicitly citing the 50% Section 232 tariff, though it has not disclosed how it will power the site and local environmental groups have raised sulphur-dioxide objections, so treat the date as an announced target. Century's Mt. Holly expansion is complete, taking the plant to full capacity for the first time since 2015, and Grundartangi Line 2 is near full. Alcoa's Portland restart lifted shipments 18% to 726,000 t. EGA continues restoring Al Taweelah cell by cell. AND THE INCENTIVE HAS INTENSIFIED: Hindalco's record print, Century's guidance beat and Maaden's Q2-2026 revenue and net-profit growth confirm this pipeline is being executed into the best margin environment in a decade, which is exactly the condition under which supply responses accelerate rather than slip.

THE DIPLOMATIC TRIGGER HAS NOW BEEN DISOWNED BY TEHRAN AT TWO LEVELS OF THE STATE INSIDE 24 HOURS, WHICH FURTHER LOWERS THE NEAR-TERM DOWNSIDE-SHOCK RISK WITHOUT REMOVING IT. Iran and Oman agreed the coordinates of a proposed Hormuz routing on 05-August and the joint statement remains unsigned with no start date. On 08-August an IRGC spokesman said reopening 'has its own specific mechanism and has nothing to do with the negotiations between Iran and Oman'; on 09-August the government said the talks were nearing agreement but warned any arrangement would NOT lead to an immediate reopening, rejected direct negotiations with the United States for now citing breaches of the June interim deal, and held to demands for an end to the naval blockade, sanctions relief and compensation. Six sessions on there has still been no measurable change in any physical observable - Kpler reports fewer than ten transits a day against roughly 130 pre-war with some vessels going dark, war-risk cover still 3-10% of hull value against about 0.25% pre-war, and no curtailed Gulf capacity restarted. The LME curve gave up $35/t of prompt structure on the announcement and has taken none of it back, so a large part of any reopening is arguably already in the price. WHAT KEEPS THIS RISK ALIVE, AND IT IS THE SINGLE MOST BEARISH ITEM ON THE TAPE: unconfirmed reports after Friday's settlement that the US could lift its naval blockade once commercial shipping resumes without restrictions - on Iran's own account the actual reopening trigger. The 17-June precedent is on the official record: official cash fell from $3,855.00 to $3,061.50, -20.6%.

THE COST FLOOR IS RISING AGAIN ON BOTH LEGS FOR THE FIRST TIME IN A WEEK. The energy leg resumed: Brent climbed above $84/bbl on Monday for a THIRD consecutive session of gains, marked at $84.27 (+0.86%) with intraday trade near $84.50 (+1.13%), WTI at $78.89 (+0.91%) and European TTF gas at EUR 56.46 (+1.65%), with the advance attributed directly to Hormuz uncertainty. Power is 30-40% of smelter cash cost, so this lifts the industry floor and feeds the carbon block with a one-to-two-cycle lag. THE RAW-MATERIAL LEG NEVER STOPPED: SMM's imported bauxite index at $71.57/mt on 06-August (+$0.70 w/w), Guinea sellers at $72-73 against refinery bids of $70-71, August long-term contracts unsettled and rumoured higher, freight to China up to about $35/mt, 30,000 mt of alumina transacted at $356/mt FOB East Australia on 05-August, and the Baltic Dry Index at 3,089 on 07-August for a sixth consecutive gain. THE CORROBORATION IS INDEPENDENT, REPEATED AND SPLIT BY INTEGRATION: Century, which buys alumina, cited unfavourable raw-material realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for a second consecutive quarter; Hindalco, integrated through bauxite, alumina and power, absorbed guided 5% sequential cost inflation and posted a record; Maaden's Q2-2026 gross profit fell 4% and operating profit 8% on input and logistics cost inflation even as revenue rose 16%. A rising LME is not converting one-for-one into margin for the non-integrated smelter.

THE CROSS-COMPLEX CONFIRMATION BROKE ON 07-AUGUST AND HAS NOT YET BEEN REPAIRED. On 06-August the whole base complex rose together and copper printed a fresh 2026 high at $14,455.00 cash, which was a genuine argument that aluminium's rebound sat inside a broad industrial bid. On 07-August copper gave back $215.00 to $14,240.00, zinc fell $72.00 to $3,785.00 and lead $10.50 to $1,840.50; only nickel (+$150.00) and aluminium advanced. Aluminium made its cycle high essentially alone. Monday's independent CFD board has reopened MIXED rather than repaired - zinc $3,710.75 (+0.36%), lead $1,894.75 (+0.13%), nickel $16,945.00 (-0.15%) - and aluminium has no Monday CFD print at all, so the complex offers no directional lead into the ring. A rally confirmed neither by its own term structure nor by its peer complex is materially narrower than the flat price suggests, and narrow rallies retrace fastest on a headline. THE FAIR COUNTERWEIGHT: copper's exchange stock nonetheless drew a further 3,675 t to 222,975 t, a fifth consecutive draw and 73,650 t below the 17-July level, so the copper setback was a price move rather than a change in the physical balance. The industrial deficit narrative is intact; the momentum confirmation is not.

CHINESE DOWNSTREAM DEMAND REMAINS THE WEAK LINK, ALTHOUGH THE POLICY CEILING IS STILL DOING MORE WORK THAN DEMAND ON THE PRICE. The official NBS manufacturing PMI is in contraction at 49.2 against the private RatingDog gauge at 50.9, and the high-temperature off-season is cutting cast-alloy operating rates and orders. What has not changed is the supply side of the same market: China has effectively reached its 45 Mt policy ceiling, with 2025 output at 45.02 Mt and H1-2026 at 22.34 Mt, and industry commentary describes room for expansion as exhausted. Domestic pricing is rotating to regional flows, lifting the South China premium on a southwest conversion surge, and net exports are down roughly 700,000 t year-to-date. Weak Chinese demand now depresses Chinese premiums more than it depresses the LME, because the metal is not leaving in the volumes it used to. Shanghai equities gained 1.02% on Monday, which is a risk-tone datapoint rather than a demand one.

THE Q4 MJP PREMIUM NEGOTIATION KEEPS ACCUMULATING BUYERS' ARGUMENTS AND THEY ARE CURVE-BASED, WHICH MAKES THEM DURABLE RATHER THAN RHETORICAL. Four consecutive sessions without a prompt premium, two of them outright contangos, is a publicly verifiable buyers' argument that did not exist a week ago; a yen near 158.06 raises the local-currency cost of any dollar premium and reinforces it. Sellers still hold the harder physical facts: exchange stock at 256,400 t after 28 draws and the lowest this century, Alba's Lines 1-3 still shut with Q2 output down 61% year-on-year, EGA restoring 1,262 cells one at a time, no signed joint statement, no measurable change in transit counts, and a weekend that produced a missile strike inside the strait and an explicit Iranian statement that the route deal is not a reopening. Talks are expected to open around late August off an 11-year-high $395/t Q3 settlement; the scenario range carried here is $315-415 and is a construct, not an assessment.

MONETARY POLICY RISK HAS EASED AT THE MARGIN ON A SOFT US JOBS PRINT. The dollar is holding the decline it took on weak payroll data - DXY about 99.67, up a marginal 0.13% on the session but below its pre-print level - with gold at about $4,322.78 and silver at $63.19 both holding gains on the same report, the classic signature of a market taking rate-hike risk out of the front end. The Fed held 9-3 on 29-July with three dissents FOR a hike; Governor Cook has said she would support hikes if disinflation does not resume while allowing that inflation may ease enough to avoid them, and June core PCE at +0.1% month-on-month and 3.3% year-on-year leans dovish. The soft labour print reinforces the dovish side; the three-session energy rally cuts the other way on the inflation arithmetic, so the net effect is a modest easing rather than a clean one. A softer dollar is a mild tailwind for dollar-denominated metal. Decision point: the 15-16 September FOMC with dots. US 10-year 4.669%.

THE RED SEA CONSTRAINT IS SEPARATE FROM HORMUZ, IS NOT ADDRESSED BY THE ROUTING AGREEMENT, AND DETERIORATED AGAIN ON SUNDAY. Houthi forces struck Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery with a drone in the early hours of 09-August; the Saudi energy ministry said the fire was extinguished with no injuries. The group framed it as retaliation for alleged Saudi drone incursions over Saada and Hajjah, it came two days after Saudi Arabia signed a defence pact with Turkey and Pakistan, and the Houthis separately claimed an attack on a Yemeni port. That follows a deadly attack on Marib, a strike on Najran and two claimed attacks on Saudi-linked tankers in the preceding days. Bab al-Mandeb is the leg that carries Gulf and Asian metal into Rotterdam via Suez, so even a full Hormuz reopening would not restore the European delivered chain. Simultaneous disruption at both chokepoints forces routing via the Cape of Good Hope, lengthening transit and raising freight and insurance. Independently of geopolitics the Baltic Dry Index reached 3,089 on 07-August, a sixth consecutive gain from 2,732 on 01-August. That is a freight cost increase a Hormuz reopening would not reverse, and it puts a floor under European delivered premiums the market may be discounting.

The Westmetall ENGLISH and GERMAN overviews were fetched independently with cache-busting queries and agree exactly on the 07-August board - all six metals, all six stock lines and all three FX fixings. That is a second consecutive clean cross-check after the English-page cache divergence documented on 04-August. Both language versions are cited separately in the sources list.

PREMIUM ASSESSMENTS ARE PERIODIC, NOT DAILY, AND ARE CARRIED AT THEIR ASSESSMENT DATES. The MJP Q3-2026 settlement of $395/t CIF Japan was assessed on 06-July-2026. The Q4-2026 figure is a SCENARIO RANGE of $315-415 and is a construct, not an assessment - no public producer offers, negotiation levels or settlement coverage dated after 06-July-2026 were found at this refresh.

THE US PREMIUM DECOMPOSITION IS ARITHMETIC, NOT AN ASSESSMENT. The tariff leg is calculated mechanically as the verified Section 232 rate multiplied by the carried LME cash. No split of the residual premium into freight, financing and tightness is published because no public assessment supports one.

ONE MATERIAL ITEM ON THIS BOARD IS REPORTED RATHER THAN CONFIRMED AND IS LABELLED AS SUCH THROUGHOUT: reports after Friday's settlement that the US could lift its naval blockade once commercial shipping through the strait resumes without restrictions. Neither government has announced this. It is carried because it is material to the bear case, not because it is established.

THE INTERNATIONAL ALUMINIUM INSTITUTE FIGURE CITED HERE IS THE JUNE-2026 RELEASE (published 20-July-2026, global primary output down 1.5% year-on-year). A widely repeated 'outside-China output down 6.7% year-on-year in July' line appears in third-party commentary but could not be traced to a dated IAI release at this refresh, so it is not carried as a sourced statistic on this board. The July IAI release is due around 20-August.

THE MAADEN (1211) EARNINGS-HISTORY STRIP WAS CORRECTED THIS RUN, AND THE CORRECTION IS STATED OPENLY RATHER THAN SILENTLY APPLIED. The prior strip carried Q2-2025 at SAR 3.47bn, which is in fact the H1-2025 net profit. Standalone Q2-2025 net profit was SAR 1.92bn. Rather than publish a mixed-basis series the Q2-2025 point was dropped and the strip now runs Q3-25 through Q2-26 on a consistent single-quarter basis, with Q2-2026 added at SAR 2.18bn.

EARNINGS-HISTORY STRIPS CONTAIN ONLY EXACT, PUBLICLY VERIFIED FIGURES. Where a period has not been reported or is not separately disclosed, the gap is left as a gap. Nothing is interpolated, derived by assumption or estimated. Chalco's Q2-2026 is absent because the H1-2026 interim has not been published; Rio Tinto's H2-2025 aluminium underlying EBITDA is absent because no separately published figure was retrievable.

INPUT-BASKET SPARKLINES CARRY ONLY PUBLICLY SOURCED MARKS ON A SINGLE STATED BASIS PER ROW. Periodic marks produce sparse two-to-three point series and that is correct rather than a defect. Rows with no public series - smelter electricity, cathode and graphite blocks, Ti-B grain refiner - carry empty histories and their source notes say why. No point on any sparkline is interpolated.

THE COPPER SPARKLINE DID NOT ROLL THIS RUN AND THAT IS CORRECT: it tracks the same 15 LME official cash sessions as the base-metals board, and no session has traded since 07-August. It will roll on today's 13:20 official.

ALUMINIUM FLUORIDE AND CRYOLITE HAVE NOT CARRIED A PUBLIC SMM WEEKLY MARK SINCE 25-JUNE-2026 and are held at that date rather than rolled forward. Silicon and magnesium last printed 06-August. Prebaked anodes and coal tar pitch settle on monthly cycles around the 17th-18th and carry July-2026 and June-2026 marks respectively.

EVERYTHING PUBLISHED HERE IS PUBLIC AND SOURCED. No confidential, internal or company-specific commercial information appears anywhere on this board - no realised prices, net-backs, shipping lanes, volumes, costs or internal commentary. The only company-specific content is publicly listed-company disclosure in the peer-earnings, earnings-history and producer-status panels, all of which cite public disclosures or press.

THE ELLIOTT WAVE SECTION IS TECHNICAL CONTEXT, NOT ADVICE, AND ITS PIVOTS ARE CONFIRMED HISTORICAL POINTS ONLY. Projections are scenarios with stated invalidation levels. No count is re-labelled without a stated invalidation break, and the daily and weekly counts share the same prices at shared pivots.

NOTHING ON THIS PAGE IS INVESTMENT, TRADING, LEGAL OR FINANCIAL ADVICE. It is a public-source market intelligence summary. Figures are as published by the cited sources at the time of compile and may be revised by those sources.
